components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Understand how Earth recycles its water through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

components.title: Overview
components.text: Water is constantly moving around our planet in a continuous journey known as the hydrologic cycle. Let's break down the three primary phases.

components.title: Evaporation and Transpiration
components.body: The sun heats up water in oceans, rivers, and lakes, causing it to change from a liquid into water vapor (gas) and rise into the atmosphere. Plants also release moisture from their leaves in a process called transpiration.

components.title: Condensation
components.body: As water vapor rises high into the cooler air, it cools down and turns back into tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals. These droplets gather around microscopic particles in the air to form clouds and fog.

components.title: Precipitation and Collection
components.body: When the water droplets in clouds become too heavy to stay suspended in the air, they fall back to Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This precipitation collects in rivers, lakes, and oceans, ready to start the cycle all over again.

components.title: Worked Example: A Puddle on a Sunny Day
components.body:
Have you ever noticed a puddle disappear a few hours after it stops raining? That is the water cycle in miniature!

1. Heat from the sun supplies energy.
2. Liquid water molecules absorb the heat and evaporate into the air.
3. The puddle dries up entirely, and the water enters the invisible vapor phase.
components.code:
# Conceptual Water Balance
total_water = evaporation + transpiration
clouds = condensation(total_water)
precipitation = clouds.drop() if clouds.weight > threshold else None
components.code_caption: Simplified physical simulation of phase change
components.takeaway: Phase changes are driven by thermal energy transfer from the sun.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapor using heat from the sun?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process where liquid water absorbs thermal energy and converts into gas.

questions.question: How do clouds form in the atmosphere?
options: Water vapor cools and condenses into tiny droplets
Ice melts directly on floating dust
Rain falls upward from mountain peaks
Oceans splash moisture into outer space
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when warm water vapor rises, cools down, and forms liquid droplets around particles.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all forms of precipitation that fall from heavy clouds.
